title: Why Your Family Pays Everyone Back Except You

beats.text: Your brother owes you three thousand dollars—but somehow, every bill gets paid except yours.
Then your tire blows, and you realize your own money is keeping you broke.
Dave gets repaid without destroying the family—but the fix starts with one question nobody asked.
In April, Danny's car died. Dave sent his emergency fund. The contract? A pizza emoji. No date.
Danny pays lenders first. They can add fees or hurt his credit. Dave can't punish his brother, so he waits.
Then Dave's tire blows. He puts four hundred dollars on his own card. The loan is hurting him now.
Guess: how many lenders lose money? Bankrate's twenty twenty-five survey: forty-four percent. Nearly one in two.
Danny may be broke, not evil. But with no date or plan, Dave is the easiest bill to postpone.
The IRS says evidence helps prove a loan wasn't a gift. A written note beats a pizza emoji.
Dave calls privately. They write three thousand dollars, one hundred twenty-five monthly, the day after payday, for two years. Both sign. Danny automates it.
Now Dave has a place in the payday line. Before lending, he asks: gift or loan? If losing it would hurt, say no—or give only what you can afford to lose.
One question. One page. No family courtroom. Subscribe for more money traps, explained through Dave's disasters.
